abstract.text: Occlusion relationship reasoning based on convolution neural networks consists of two subtasks: occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. Due to the essential differences between the two subtasks in the feature expression at the higher and lower stages, it is challenging to carry on them simultaneously in one network. To address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower stages. Besides, considering the restriction of occlusion orientation presentation to occlusion orientation learning, we design a new orthogonal representation for occlusion orientation and proposed the Orthogonal Orientation Regression loss which can get rid of the unfitness between occlusion representation and learning and further prompt the occlusion orientation learning. Finally, we apply a multi-scale loss together with our proposed orientation regression loss to guide the boundary and orientation path learning respectively. Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

evidence.quote: Deng et al. [2] use a bottom-up/top-down architecture to predict crisp boundaries.
In our network, as shown in Fig. 2, we use ResNet [6] as a base feature extraction model as in previous works [18, 11, 10].

predecessors.why: The paper adopts a bottom-up/top-down encoder-decoder design and ResNet backbone, building on these prior architectures.

evidence.quote: Previous methods, such as DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10] first use the backbone network to extract different level features and use the entire decoder to extract shared information for two tasks, which improve the effect of occlusion reasoning but ignores the different effects of different level features on boundary and orientation.

predecessors.why: The DDNet design is positioned against these prior two-task occlusion networks and their unified decoder.

evidence.quote: Previous methods, such as DOOBNet [18], OFNet [10] first use the backbone network to extract different level features and use the entire decoder to extract shared information for two tasks, which improve the effect of occlusion reasoning but ignores the different effects of different level features on boundary and orientation.

targets.why: The paper critiques that sharing the entire decoder ignores how higher- and lower-stage features contribute differently to boundary and orientation tasks.

evidence.quote: Previous methods [19, 18, 10] infer the occlusion orientation by regressing a continuous orientation value. However, due to the periodicity of the occlusion orientation itself, predicting the occlusion orientation based on the continuous orientation value is difficult for the network.

targets.why: The paper argues that continuous orientation regression suffers from the periodicity problem.

evidence.quote: To address this issue, we propose a novel Dual-path Decoder Network, which uniformly extracts occlusion information at higher stages and separates into two paths to recover boundary and occlusion orientation respectively in lower stages.
Experiments demonstrate that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art results on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets.

sections.summary: The paper addresses occlusion relationship reasoning, which consists of occlusion boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference. It argues that these two subtasks should share high-level occlusion information but be separated at lower stages because they require different spatial features, and that existing methods suffer from the periodicity of orientation regression. The introduction outlines the DDNet dual-path decoder and orthogonal orientation representation as solutions, while the related work reviews encoder-decoder, multi-scale supervision, and orientation prediction methods.
sections.title: Motivation and Related Work

source_span.end_text: Feature Fusion and Separation Block: We use the Feature Fusion and Separation module to connect the various stages of the decoder.
source_span.start_text: In this section, we first introduce the proposed DDNet, which contains a dual-path decoder structure and the multi-scale supervision structure for boundary path.

sections.summary: The DDNet uses a dual-path decoder that shares an occlusion-shared module at higher stages and then splits into boundary and orientation paths at lower stages. The boundary path uses a layer-by-layer decoder with multi-scale supervision via Feature Fusion and Separation blocks, while the orientation path uses skip connections. Auxiliary blocks include the Occlusion-shared Module, Feature Boost Residual Block, and Feature Fusion and Separation Block.
sections.title: DDNet Architecture

source_span.end_text: In CNN-based methods of occlusion relationship reasoning, the object boundary extraction and occlusion orientation inference are trained simultaneously.
source_span.start_text: We define a new orthogonal occlusion orientation representation, which decomposes the orientation orthogonally into a horizontal vector ~a = (a, 0) and a vertical vector ~b = (0, b) as the Fig. 4.

sections.summary: The paper proposes representing occlusion orientation as a pair of orthogonal vectors, which avoids the periodicity problem of continuous angle regression. Based on this representation, it defines the Orthogonal Orientation Regression (OOR) loss. The overall training loss combines boundary loss (class-balanced cross-entropy with multi-scale side supervision) and orientation loss computed only on boundary pixels.
sections.title: Orthogonal Orientation Regression and Training

source_span.end_text: Performance on BSDS ownership: The BSDS ownership is difficult to train due to the small number of the training samples.
source_span.start_text: We evaluate the proposed approach on two public datasets: PIOD [19] and BSDS ownership dataset [13].

sections.summary: The method is evaluated on PIOD and BSDS ownership datasets. Implementation uses ResNet50 backbone, AdamW optimizer, and specific hyperparameters. Evaluation metrics are BPR and OPR with ODS, OIS, and AP. The DDNet outperforms recent methods like DOC, DOOBNet, and OFNet on both datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results.

source_span.start_text: In this section, we conduct experiments on PIOD dataset to study the impact of parameters and verify each component in our network.

sections.summary: Ablation studies on PIOD validate the design choices: sharing top-2 stages is optimal; predicting orthogonal vectors outperforms continuous orientation regression; multi-scale supervision with multiple side outputs improves performance. The conclusion summarizes the DDNet, its dual-path decoder, multi-scale supervision, and OOR loss. Qualitative results in Figure 7 show clearer boundaries and orientation than DOOBNet and OFNet.
